title: Victoria's Antimatter to feature 10 days of the 'finest moving image art' from around the world
excerpt: From Oct. 15 to 25, work from around the world will be screened in an intimate downtown gallery space
content:
Published 5:30 am Friday, October 2, 2026

By Victoria News Staff

Antimatter is bringing 10 days of the “finest moving image art’ from around the world to downtown Victoria for its 29th annual festival.

From Oct. 15 to 25, work from around the world will be screened in an intimate downtown gallery space adapted to a black box microcinema. A total of 21 programs and 136 artists’ films from 31 countries will be featured over the 10 days.

Evening and afternoon in-person screenings at Deluge Contemporary Art (636 Yates St) are followed by free, global streaming access the following day for 24 hours at the Antimatter website.

Festival offerings can be experienced in person, online, and in public.

“We built this festival over three decades, adapting to changes and refining our focus while always championing the artists behind the work and never giving in to populism or shying away from the complex, enigmatic and challenging nature of the art form we represent,” says festival director Todd Eacrett.

“Our networks are extensive and venerable, informed and developed by the new voices we amplify every iteration of the festival. Every year, more filmmakers attend the festival and contribute to the larger discussions around what we do, inviting the public entre into this exciting world.”

Notable films representing the breadth of approaches employed by festival artists include Contact, a film by documentarian Jonathan Walley, chronicling Derek Nelson—fabricator, activist, BMX pro and artist—as he transforms an entire skatepark into a playable musical instrument where skate, BMX, art and music scenes collide, and Null Adjustments, a love letter to the analog by Andrew Northrup which follows the repair of the Buchla 100 at the Library of Congress, an early modular synthesizer built by Don Buchla for composer Morton Subotnick, who used it to create Silver Apples of the Moon.

Nada El-Omari’s Momentum considers what memories gain as time moves, in which 20 years after it was recorded, the course of a day resurfaces. In The Stars Watch from Long Ago from legendary filmmaker Stacey Steers, a tiny farmhouse spins through the cosmos, carrying silent film icon Lillian Gish into the vast unknown.

Automat, a series of filmic self-portraits by participants, introduces audiences to the creative process and lives of media artists via their own words and images, providing nuance and context for their creative output. This year Automat will offer dozens of new introductions to the individuals behind the work, all available at the festival website.

Media installations by Winston Hacking, Lilan Yang, Bocheng Zhang and Kelly Egan will be on view at Legacy Gallery, the Window Gallery in Millie’s Lane and the transom window and entrance foyer of Deluge Contemporary Art.

Advance screening tickets and festival passes can be purchased on the Antimatter website with discounts for students and older adults.

Installations and online streaming programs are free or by donation. The complete schedule and festival program guide are available at antimatter.ca.
